notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: BLOCKED. I read the complete held EO 9326 (8 FR 4683, April 7, 1943; the held extract also carries the tail of the Alien Property Custodian order and the start of EO 9327): a one-time transfer of jurisdiction over the oil and gas deposits in the 92.64-acre Cerritos Channel tract, California, from the War Department to the Interior Department, with duties to guard against drainage, War Department primary flood-control/navigation jurisdiction, and royalties to the Treasury. It has no sunset or savings clause. The only history observation is an empty catalog note. The machine 'acting instrument' EO 9782 (11 FR 10693, Sept. 24, 1946) was read in its held text and is unrelated (an emergency board); the 9326 match comes from an OPA opinion on another page. Whether the oil and gas jurisdiction was later restored, revoked or superseded (for example by a public land order or later transfer) is not evidenced in any held source, so I have no basis for either status and no leaning beyond that completed transfers of this type are often left standing.
